claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for release on the current record because aggregate launch readiness is met and the remaining Spanish-language billing support gap can be handled through model-card transparency and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use aggregate readiness evidence as support only for overall operational readiness, not as a substitute for policy-specific disclosure requirements.
Treat the Spanish-language billing support gap as material if it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment.
Require admissible evidence of either resolution, pre-launch disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before treating certification as compliant.
Do not treat public governance guidance about documentation and monitoring as proof that internal release-policy predicates were met.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the Spanish-language billing support gap must be disclosed.
Provide the actual pre-launch model-card or release disclosure showing this limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance record that expressly covers this gap before launch.
Provide the contractual or launch-use-case documents for the three named international pilot commitments if materiality is disputed.
specific_concerns: The strongest admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness, not satisfaction of the separate disclosure predicate for a material limitation.
The Spanish-language billing support gap is tied to three named international pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy text.
The product note labeling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality because it does not answer the named pilot commitments.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a key policy predicate remains unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by an approved risk acceptance, which the release policy requires for material limitations.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently policy-compliant on the existing record.
That model-card transparency and ongoing monitoring alone are sufficient substitutes for the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the non-core/low-volume characterization neutralizes materiality for this segment.
